evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to select favorite teams and preferred sports channels, and use these selections to filter and display a personalized news feed.
evaluations.feedback: Mostly faithful to the source and reasonably testable. Good combination of favorite teams and preferred channels into one coherent function. However, 'personalized news feed' is an interpretation not stated explicitly in the source; the source says users can display current news of favorite teams and select preferred channels, but does not clearly define a single feed behavior or whether filtering is conjunctive, disjunctive, or separately configurable. Acceptance criteria are too thin for production BDD: no coverage of editing selections, no behavior when no favorites/channels are selected, no persistence across sessions, and no handling of conflicting filters. Improve by splitting selection/persistence from feed filtering if needed, and specify exact filtering logic and fallback behavior.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide live ticker functionality allowing users to follow the live results of their favorite teams in real time.
evaluations.feedback: Strong requirement with clear traceability to the source. The wording is specific, testable, and aligned with the described live ticker module and real-time updates. The acceptance criterion is understandable, but it could still be stronger by defining what 'real-time' means operationally, expected refresh/update interval, and behavior when no live match exists. Also consider adding scenarios for network loss and resumed synchronization, since the source discusses degraded/offline operation. Still, as a generated requirement, this is one of the best.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must cover and display news, results, and data for all football leagues and competitions, both national and international.
evaluations.feedback: Captures the broad source intent but is too absolute and therefore weak as an implementable requirement. 'All football leagues and competitions' is unbounded, hard to verify, and depends on external data availability. 'News, results, and data' is also vague because 'data' is undefined. The acceptance criterion introduces 'fixtures,' which are not explicitly stated in the requirement text. This requirement violates good atomicity and feasibility principles. Improve by defining the supported competition catalogue, data domains per competition, update frequency, and exceptions where third-party providers do not supply coverage.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide detailed information on teams and individual players that is accessible at any time.
evaluations.feedback: The requirement is traceable but too vague to be considered production-ready. 'Detailed information' is undefined, and 'accessible at any time' is ambiguous because the app also operates under limited/offline network conditions. Acceptance criteria add 'stats and background,' which may be reasonable but are not explicitly grounded in the source. To improve, enumerate the minimum required attributes for teams and players, define freshness expectations, and clarify whether 'at any time' means 24/7 service availability, offline cached access, or simple navigational availability.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must integrate live stream links from providers (such as DAZN or Sky Sport) and display these links only when a live broadcast is available and transmission rights are fulfilled for the user's country.
evaluations.feedback: Accurate, well-scoped, and strongly traceable to the source. It preserves the key legal/display conditions and does not overreach beyond link integration. The acceptance criterion is solid BDD-style and captures the main path. For even better precision, define how country eligibility is determined, what happens when rights cannot be verified, whether links disappear after the broadcast ends, and whether provider deep links or in-app web views are expected. Still, this is a high-quality requirement.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide an in-app notification system that sends users real-time updates for current events, news, or results related to their followed teams, once the function is activated.
evaluations.feedback: Good traceability and generally testable. However, 'in-app notification system' may be slightly misleading because the acceptance criterion refers to push notifications on the device; the source says the app is linked to a notification system, which could include push notifications but does not strictly say 'in-app' only. 'Real-time' is again undefined. 'Current events' is vague and could include goals, red cards, match start, final whistle, injuries, etc. Improve by specifying notification channels, opt-in/opt-out behavior, supported event types, delivery expectations, and behavior for multiple followed teams.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must provide a streamlined registration and login process that can be completed directly at app startup.
evaluations.feedback: Reasonably aligned with the source, but 'streamlined' and 'uncomplicated' are subjective and weakly testable. The acceptance criterion introduces 'within 2 minutes' and 'simple steps,' neither of which comes from the source and both need measurable definitions if retained. Also unclear whether registration/login is mandatory at startup or merely available there. To improve, specify whether users can skip authentication, the allowed authentication methods, maximum number of screens/fields, and success/error flows. As written, it is understandable but not robust.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to share news and game reports directly from the app to social media platforms.
evaluations.feedback: Faithful and testable at a high level. The requirement is clear, but 'social media platforms' is broad and could lead to implementation ambiguity across Android and iOS sharing capabilities. The acceptance criterion is minimal and only verifies presentation of sharing options, not successful handoff of content, formatting of shared payload, or permission/error handling. Improve by clarifying whether native OS share sheets are acceptable, whether deep integration with named platforms is required, and what content types/metadata must be shared.

evaluations.requirement_text: The system must allow users to individually configure modules and connect their own interface to the user interface for personalized experience.
evaluations.feedback: This is the weakest functional requirement because it reproduces source ambiguity without resolving it. 'Configure modules' is somewhat plausible, but 'connect their own interface to the user interface' is highly unclear and sounds more like architecture wording than a user-facing feature. The acceptance criterion narrows it to reordering/toggling modules, which is a useful interpretation, but that behavior is not actually stated in the requirement text. This requirement is not sufficiently precise, atomic, or testable. It should be rewritten entirely: either define explicit personalization capabilities such as enable/disable/reorder dashboard modules, or discard the 'own interface' phrasing unless the product truly supports custom UI plugins/themes/layouts.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must be fully loaded and ready to use within a maximum of two seconds after starting.
evaluations.feedback: Excellent extraction from the source. Clear, measurable, and directly testable. The acceptance criterion is appropriate, though it would benefit from defining the test environment more precisely: device classes, OS versions, network state, cold vs warm start, and what counts as 'main content displayed and usable.' Still, this is a strong non-functional requirement with clear verification potential.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must function reliably even with limited network coverage, providing graceful degradation of features.
evaluations.feedback: Good capture of the source intent and a sensible refinement via graceful degradation. However, 'limited network coverage,' 'reliably,' and 'critical features' are all underspecified. The acceptance criterion introduces 'news, results last known state' which is a fair inference, but should be backed by explicit offline/cache rules. Improve by defining network conditions (e.g., bandwidth/latency thresholds), the exact features that must remain available, retry behavior, timeout thresholds, and required user messaging for unavailable live capabilities.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must remain usable offline, allowing access to core features and last-known data if the connection is lost temporarily.
evaluations.feedback: This is aligned with the source and more testable than many others. Still, 'usable offline' and 'core features' are ambiguous. The acceptance criterion is directionally good but does not define what data must be cached, how stale data is labeled, how long offline access should last, or whether the app must support actions offline that later sync. Also overlaps somewhat with NFR-002, so the boundary between degraded connectivity and full offline mode should be clarified. Improve by specifying the offline feature set and cache retention behavior.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must support at least 100,000 simultaneous users without any loss of performance.
evaluations.feedback: Traceable, but not well engineered as written. 'Without any loss of performance' is unrealistic and not measurable unless a baseline and SLOs are defined. Also unclear whether this refers to backend service capacity, concurrent active sessions, or simultaneously connected clients across all app services. The acceptance criterion repeats the same ambiguity using 'as responsive as normal.' Improve by defining concurrency model, target latency/error-rate thresholds under load, affected operations, geographic assumptions, and performance measurement methodology.

evaluations.requirement_text: All application modules and the user interface must remain consistent and operational even if the external server providing data is updated.
evaluations.feedback: Reasonably derived from the source, but still ambiguous. 'External server is updated' could mean API version changes, data refreshes, infrastructure changes, or schema modifications. 'Remain consistent and operational' is not specific enough for verification. The acceptance criterion also says 'function as before with no visible disruption,' which is desirable but vague. Improve by specifying backward compatibility expectations, API contract/versioning requirements, tolerance to non-breaking backend changes, and failure behavior when contract-breaking changes occur.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must undergo thorough testing and support processes before release to identify and resolve technical problems early.
evaluations.feedback: This is not a product quality attribute requirement so much as a generic process statement. 'Thorough testing' and 'support processes' are subjective and non-verifiable without defined gates. The acceptance criterion refers to QA and defect correction but still lacks measurable release criteria. This should be rewritten as concrete quality gate requirements, such as minimum automated test coverage, zero open critical defects before release, crash-free session targets in staging, or mandatory regression suite pass rates.

evaluations.requirement_text: User feedback and app reviews must be continuously evaluated to improve app functionality.
evaluations.feedback: Again, this is a process/product management statement rather than a system non-functional requirement. 'Continuously evaluated' is vague and not objectively testable. The acceptance criterion about planning and tracking improvements is project governance, not software behavior or quality constraints. If retained, convert it into a measurable operational process requirement, such as review cadence, SLA for triage, categorization workflow, or dashboard/reporting obligations.

evaluations.requirement_text: All personal user data must be processed in compliance with the GDPR.
evaluations.feedback: Strong and faithful legal/compliance requirement. It is high value, but still too broad to verify as a single requirement because GDPR compliance spans consent, lawful basis, minimization, retention, access, rectification, erasure, portability, breach handling, and more. The acceptance criterion lists examples but remains very high level. Improve by decomposing into specific compliance requirements and adding explicit auditable controls, such as consent capture, privacy notice presentation, export/delete workflows, and records of processing.

evaluations.requirement_text: The application must be deployable and fully functional on both Android and iOS mobile operating systems.
evaluations.feedback: Correctly derived from the source and generally testable. However, 'fully functional' can be problematic because feature parity may be limited by platform-specific constraints. Also missing target OS versions, device classes, and store distribution expectations. The acceptance criterion is acceptable, but should define supported versions, key compatibility scenarios, and any permitted platform deviations. Good requirement overall, but it needs tighter compatibility boundaries for real verification.
